pairs.evidence: apps/stage/src/avatar/layers.ts:177 When a rig's layers.json loads but one of the PNGs it names returns 404, fetchRig builds an error that names the file, but loadForm's 404 filter drops it without a log and draws the placeholder, so a broken rig looks the same as having no rig at all.

techniques.evidence: apps/stage/src/avatar/layers.ts:177 The 404 exemption is meant for 'no rig', but it also matches '<file>.png: HTTP 404' from line 156, so a missing named input ends in a quiet default with no named error.

apps/stage/src/avatar/layers.ts:156 The loader never assembles a partial rig: any missing layer file rejects the whole form, so no gap is papered over inside the picture. The defect is only that the rejection is then hidden (line 177).

pairs.registryProposal: silent-defects-get-a-code-or-an-error is written for compiled compositions, but it applies directly to live real-time renderers that swap in a fallback asset. It could say that an exemption meant for legitimate absence ('no asset configured') must not catch partial absence ('the asset is half there').
